sanjay: Ran an nsys trace on prod-like batch job (seq_len=2048, batch=32). Seeing lots of small kernels + big cudaMemcpy DtoH spikes around kv-cache churn. Uploading link. :eyes:
ellie: Can you add NVTX ranges around the dispatcher and kernel-selector? Hard to map fallback points from kernel names alone.
ben: We already emit coarse NVTX for "kv-cache" and "dispatch", but they're too broad. Propose per-request spans like "req/<model>/<route>/<step>" and a short kernel id payload. Maybe record kv_hit as a marker.
sanjay: Quick prototype I used in C++ runtime:
```
// pre-allocated name buffer recommended
std::string name = "req:" + request_id;
nvtxRangePushA(name.c_str());
... dispatch + kernel selection ...
nvtxRangePop();
```
ellie: Love that. Two notes: 1) keep names short (<=64 chars) so perfetto labels don't truncate awkwardly, 2) avoid allocating in hot paths — pre-alloc or use string interning.
mira: Naming conv suggestion: use compact tokens, e.g. "r:mdlX/routeA/enc" or suffixes like "/ks" for kernel-selector, "/k" for kernel exec. Helps when scanning traces.
ellie: Also instrument batching heuristics: emit "batch/prepare" range around formation and NVTX counters for size and age_ms. That lets us correlate small batches with non-optimal kernels.
sanjay: I noticed a perf regression after flipping selector logic — old path used fused kernels, new path falls back to generic GEMM when seq < 128. Need to show per-request timeline when fallback happens.
ben: NVTX supports payloads via nvtxRangePushEx where we can set a 64-bit value. Put kernel_id there so GPU kernel rows in perfetto can be annotated. Example: nvtxEventAttributes_t attr; attr.version=NVTX_VERSION; attr.size=NVTX_EVENT_ATTRIB_STRUCT_SIZE; attr.payload.llVal = kernel_id; nvtxRangePushEx(&attr);
infra-bot: Trace uploaded to perf-archive: https://perf/archives/1791234567 :thumbsup:
mira: One extra caution: we saw nsys overhead spike when doing >1M nvtxRangePush/pop calls (hot loops). Prefer one span per request or per batch, not per token. For micro ops use nvtxMarkEx to mark hit/miss counters instead of full ranges.
ellie: For the KV cache specifically, instrument "kvcache/lookup" as nvtxMarkEx with a small payload (hit=1/miss=0) rather than full spans; lookups are microseconds.
sanjay: Plan: add per-request span, kernel_id payload, batch metadata tags (size/age), and a trace_id payload for correlation across CPU/GPU traces. Will run nsys+perfetto with the perf-suite and post screenshots.
ben: Also tag the git diff with "perf/trace" so infra can pick it up in the regression bot.
ellie: Thanks — once you push, we can run a focused trace and check whether kernel routing points align with KV-cache churn. :+1:
